lawyer:
Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud with Mr. Md. Waliur Reza Choudhury ----- for the petitioner
Mr. Rafiq-ul-Huq with Mr. Md. Mamunur Rashid ----- for the respondent No. 3
parties:
M/s. Uttara Properties Ltd.
Vs.
Joint District Judge and Artharin Adalat No.1, Dhaka and others
full_judgment:
Md. Awlad Ali, J: This Rule arises out of an order dated 12.7.2005 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 55/2005 by Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka arising out of Money Execution Case No. 417/2003. 

 2. Briefly stated, the facts are that the petitioner is a Private Limited Company engaged in the business of Real Estates of which Mr. Matiur Rahman is the Chairman and Managing Director. The respondent No.2 Agrani bank and its Mohakali Branch instituted Title Suit No. 79/89 in the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka impleading one Momtaz Begum and her husband Mohammad Salim as sole defendants praying for a decree for realisation of Tk. 11,33,946.60 as on 31.03.89 with 20% interest and obtained a preliminary decree on 12.05.1991 which was made final on 24.06.2003. The decree holder bank put the decree in Execution being Artha Jari (Money Execution) Case No. 417/2003. In the execution proceedings auction sale notice was published in the Daily Ittefaq on 8.6.2005 fixing 14.7.2005 the date of auction sale of the property which included the property of the petitioner. Thereafter, the petitioner sent one of their officers to the Court to know about the matter and after search through the said officer came to learn that the auction sale notice has been published under section 33(4) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in Arthajari Case No. 417/2003 and also came to know that previously a suit was instituted in the Artha Rin Adalat for realisation of Tk. 11,33,946.60. The petitioner thereafter, filed an application under Order 21 Rules 58,59,60 and 62 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 11.7.2005 praying for releasing the properties from the sale proceedings in favour of the petitioner. The petitioner also on 12.7.2005 filed an application praying for stay of the proceeding of auction sale till disposal of the Miscellaneous case but the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat by impugned order dated 12.7.2005 outright dismissed the Miscellaneous case as being not maintainable for non-compliance of section 32(2) of the Arthain Adalat Ain, 2003 and also rejected the application for stay. It is against that order the petitioner obtained the Rule and also the order of stay. 

 3. The respondent No.3 bank has filed an affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia, that it is a condition precedent that a third party claimant is to furnish security to the extent of 25% of the decretal dues as contemplated under section 32(2) of the Artharin Adalat Ain, 2003 to make the application under order 21 rule 58 C.P.C maintainable, but the petitioner filed the application under order 21 rule 58 C.P. Code as 3rd party claimant without complying with the mandatory provision of law and as such the learned Judge of the Artharin Adalat rightly rejected the Miscellaneous case outright and there has been no illegality in making the order under challenge. 

 4. It is contended by Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner that so far as it relates to the furnishing of security to the extent of 25% of the decretal dues filing the application by the third party claimant under Order 21 Rule 58 he will not make any submission as this Court in other cases decided the point stating that section 32(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is not unconstitutional. But pointing out the provision of section 32(1) he has contended that since there is clear indication that the decree holder may have a right to file a written objection within 30 days to the claim filed by the third party/claimant and have the objection heard if the application is not outright rejected by the Adalat on preliminary consideration, and considering that provision the Artharin Adalat had no jurisdiction to reject the application under Order 21 Rule 58 outright on the date when the matter was fixed for hearing on maintainability without giving the petitioner a chance to furnish security as required under sub-section (2) of section 32 of the Ain. But the learned Judge, Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud contends, without giving any chance to the petitioner, fixing a date for furnishing security, rejected the application outright which is not permissible under the law. 

 5. Mr. Rafiq-ul-Huq the learned counsel appearing for the respondent Agrani bank has contended that if any application is preferred by any 3rd party claimant according to the provision of civil procedure code and the petitioner makes any claim in the property to be sold in execution case in that case he is required to furnish security at a length of 25% of the decretal dues in default of which the claim of the 3rd party petitioner may not be entertained and shall he rejected by the Adalat. Mr. Huq has referred to us a decision of this Court reported in 57 DLR 164= 25 BLD 171 where it has been held that the claim of 3rd party would attract the provision of sub-section (2) of section 32 of the Ain and under the provision of Civil Procedure Code that claim is only dealt with under order 21 rule 58 C.P. Code Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud has, however conceded to such proposition and further said that the petitioner is ready to furnish security if a chance is given to do so. 

 6. The only question to be determined by us as to whether in the facts of the present case the Adalat ought to have given any opportunity to the petitioner to furnish security as required under sub-section (2) of section 32 of the Ain before it outright rejected the application on question of maintainability. It appears from the order dated 11.7.2005 that the application under Order 21 Rule 58 and some other Rules as quoted in the application was filed by the petitioner company being a third party claimant on 11.7.2005 which was fixed on 12.7.2005 for hearing on maintainability. No written objection having been filed by the decree holder bank for having the claim heard within 30 days as indicated in sub-section (1) of section 32, but the Adalat rejected the Miscellaneous case for not furnishing security to the extent of 25% of the decretal dues with the application filed Order 21 Rule 58 C.P.C. 

 10. The learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka is directed to allow the petitioner at least 2 (two) weeks time to furnish security to the extent of 25% of the decretal dues in default the Miscellaneous Case shall stand rejected.
